objective.value: Design, evaluate (in silico) and implement novel non-natural biosynthetic routes for isopentyldiol (IPDO) production in Escherichia coli; compare a RetroPath RL-computationally designed route (route B) with the previously published route A and two intuitively designed routes (C from alpha,beta-DHIV; D from mevalonate) regarding theoretical yield, thermodynamics (MDF), energy cost, number of non-native steps and enzyme/intermediate penalties, and test their in vivo IPDO production.

hypothesis.value: A priori in silico evaluation (FBA theoretical yield + MDF thermodynamic driving force + energy cost + enzyme/intermediate penalties) can predict the relative feasibility of alternative non-natural IPDO pathways; the route with the most favorable profile (route B) is more likely to function in vivo than intuitively designed routes C and D.
hypothesis.notes: The paper does not state an explicit hypothesis sentence; this is reconstructed from the stated purpose of comparing in silico predictions with implementation results.

inference.rationale: Abstract, Introduction final paragraph and Results 2.1/4 jointly state that the study tests whether in silico criteria (FBA, MDF) predict pathway implementability; no single sentence declares a formal hypothesis.

Retrosynthesis pathway prediction: RetroPath RL (similarity cutoff 0.5, width 10, depth 7, max rollout 10, reaction rule radius 2/4/8/16, biological pathway scoring; E. coli metabolite database as sinks; second round with similarity 0.1 and random scoring)
FBA on genome-scale model iY75_1357 (E. coli K-12 W3110) with route-specific submodels iY75_1357_IPDO_A/B/C/D, glucose uptake 15 mmol/g/DCW
Thermodynamic analysis: component contribution method for DrG'0; MDF via equilibrator-api and equilibrator-pathway with defined metabolite concentration boundaries
Computational saturation mutagenesis / virtual screening of CAR based on its crystal structure (binding pocket and adjacent loop)
GC/GC-MS data analysis by retention time and spectral comparison to standards

Route B judged best overall (fewest non-native steps, no condition-dependent/uncharacterized enzymes).

experiments.purpose: Design candidate IPDO pathways (RetroPath RL) and rank routes A-D by FBA theoretical yield, MDF thermodynamics, ATP/NADPH cost, non-native steps and enzyme/intermediate penalties
experiments.host: in silico (E. coli K-12 W3110 model iY75_1357)
experiments.conditions: glucose uptake 15 mmol/g/DCW; MDF concentration boundaries per Methods 5.5
experiments.control: route A (previously published) as reference route
experiments.readout: theoretical yield, MDF, bottleneck reactions, energy cost
experiments.outcome: Route B ranked highest overall priority; route C highest yield but lowest MDF; route D highest MDF but all upstream reactions rate-limiting
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate design action (selection of route B for implementation). Q2: performed in this paper. Q3: determined which pathway was implemented and shaped all subsequent experiments.

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Pathway-level design choice: select and implement the RetroPath RL-predicted route B (HPD -> CAR -> ADH from alpha-KIC) over intuitive routes C and D.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Previously reported route A reached only 310 mg/L IPDO, far from practical requirement; in silico comparison showed route B has fewest non-native steps, high thermodynamic driving force (after removing the shared PDDH bottleneck, MDF 74.93 kJ/mol), low energy cost, and no condition-dependent or poorly characterized enzymes.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: The decision was driven by predictive tool outputs (RetroPath RL, FBA, MDF); these are computational predictions requiring experimental confirmation, which the authors then performed. Route A's 310 mg/L titer is hard prior data but from a previous study.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The paper explicitly articulates mechanistic grounds: thermodynamic driving force topology (oxidative + reductive hydroxyl formation), carbon loss via decarboxylation, ATP/NADPH burden, and enzyme substrate-affinity penalties.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When designing a non-natural pathway for IPDO (short-chain diol) production in E. coli, prioritize candidate routes that combine oxidative and reductive hydroxyl-group formation, maximize MDF while inspecting thermodynamic topology (not only the single MDF number), and minimize non-native steps and cofactor/ATP cost, because thermodynamic driving force and energy burden determine in vivo feasibility; validated only for IPDO routes in E. coli.
alternatives_considered: Route C (from alpha,beta-DHIV): highest theoretical yield but lowest MDF (6.96 kJ/mol), GDHt requires vitamin B12; implemented but produced no IPDO
Route D (from mevalonate): highest MDF but driven by one highly exergonic ADO step with all upstream reactions rate-limiting; ADO mechanism controversial; implemented but produced no IPDO
Second RetroPath RL route via ethyl 3-hydroxyisovalerate hydrolysis: rejected because the precursor is not a natural E. coli metabolite

experiments.purpose: Express and purify functional CAR and verify its activity on 3-OH-IV (route B step 2)
experiments.intervention: coexpression of car (N. iowensis) with sfp (B. subtilis) on pCDFDuet under T7 promoter
experiments.conditions: enzyme expression per Methods 5.6; activity assay 80 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, 0.25 mM NADPH, 1 mM ATP, 5 mM substrate, 100 ug CAR, 30 C
experiments.outcome: CAR active on 3-OH-IV (0.045 umol/min/mg) but >10-fold lower than on BA (0.511); CAR+Sfp coexpression crucial for activity (Table S3, supplement unavailable)
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate construct design (car+sfp coexpression cassette). Q2: constructed in this paper. Q3: the active CAR/Sfp module was reused in all downstream route implementations (IPB02, IPC01, IPD01, IPB05-07).

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Coexpression of the phosphopantetheinyl transferase Sfp with CAR to obtain fully functional enzyme (expression/activation balancing).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: CAR apoenzyme requires post-translational phosphopantetheinylation of a conserved serine to be active; authors cite prior report that Sfp from B. subtilis performs this modification (ref 22) and observed that coexpression is crucial for CAR activity (Table S3).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Text states measured activity comparison (Table S3) showing coexpression enhances CAR activity; however the underlying table is in the unavailable supplement, so direct numbers could not be verified.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The paper explicitly states the Sfp requirement 'has been reported' (Finnigan et al., ref 22) and adopted it based on that literature.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When expressing a carboxylic acid reductase (CAR) in E. coli for pathway implementation, coexpress a 4'-phosphopantetheinyl transferase such as Sfp, because CAR requires post-translational phosphopantetheinylation of its conserved serine to be catalytically functional.

experiments.purpose: Verify IPDO production from 3-OH-IV in vitro with purified CAR + YqhD (E. coli) or GRE2 (S. cerevisiae S288c)
experiments.conditions: HEPES pH 7.5, 0/20 mM 3-OH-IV, 10 mM NADPH, 2 mM ATP, 10 mM Mg2+, 400 ug CAR, 200 ug YqhD or GRE2, 30 C, 6 h
experiments.outcome: 187.2 mg/L (YqhD) and 200.0 mg/L (GRE2) IPDO; none without substrate; GRE2 slightly better than YqhD
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails as an engineering decision: this is a feasibility measurement of an already-designed step; it introduces no new design action, though its result (GRE2 >= YqhD) informed the later choice of GRE2 for in vivo constructs.

experiments.purpose: Verify in vivo IPDO production from supplemented 3-OH-IV
experiments.host: E. coli BL21(DE3), strain IPB02 (pCDF-car-sfp + pET-gre)
experiments.intervention: two-plasmid heterologous expression of car, sfp, GRE2
experiments.conditions: LB overnight seed; 10 mL FM-II, initial OD 0.1, +/- 50 mM 3-OH-IV, 0.1 mM IPTG at OD600 0.4-0.6, 30 C 200 rpm
experiments.outcome: 480.0 mg/L IPDO with 50 mM 3-OH-IV; none without
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q3 fails: validates the downstream half of route B in vivo but introduces no new engineering action beyond the constructs already designed; it confirms feasibility before pathway completion.

experiments.purpose: Identify a functional alpha-ketoisocaproate dioxygenase for alpha-KIC to 3-OH-IV conversion (route B step 1)
experiments.host: E. coli BL21(DE3), strains IPB03 (pET22b-SnHPD) and IPB04 (pET22b-AaHPD)
experiments.intervention: heterologous expression of two HPD homologs (S. noursei DSM 40635; A. albata DSM 44149) and whole-cell catalysis comparison
experiments.conditions: LB + 0.1 mM IPTG overnight; cells resuspended in 0.1 M Tris pH 6.5 + 33 mM alpha-KIC + 3 mM FeSO4 + 1 mM DTT + 5 mM ascorbate; 30 C, 220 rpm; sampling 6 and 24 h; product then converted to IPDO in vitro
experiments.control: E. coli BL21(DE3) without HPD (negative control, Table 2)
experiments.readout: 3-OH-IV produced; subsequent IPDO from in vitro cascade
experiments.outcome: No conversion in negative control; AaHPD (IPB04) gave higher 3-OH-IV than SnHPD (IPB03) at both 6 h (1294.7 vs 914.3 mg/L) and 24 h (2119.2 vs 1812.1 mg/L); AaHPD selected
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate choice between two candidate enzymes. Q2: performed here. Q3: AaHPD was carried into the final route-B strain (pTrc-cgh).

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Rate-limiting enzyme identification/engineering via homolog comparison: select the more active HPD for the alpha-KIC to 3-OH-IV step.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Route B requires an HPD active on alpha-KIC; two homologs were available as candidates and their activities differed.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Whole-cell catalysis measurements (Table 2) directly compare 3-OH-IV titers for both homologs at two time points.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: AaHPD was chosen because it empirically showed higher activity; the paper gives no mechanistic reason why AaHPD outperforms SnHPD.
alternatives_considered: SnHPD from S. noursei: lower activity, not carried forward

experiments.purpose: Improve CAR activity in the production host by optimizing CAR:Sfp expression ratio
experiments.host: E. coli W3110 with chromosomal J23105-sfp + pTrc-car (strain IPB05)
experiments.intervention: chromosomal integration of sfp under artificial constitutive promoter J23105; car overexpressed from pTrc99a
experiments.conditions: standard enzyme expression conditions; CAR activity compared across hosts/configurations (Table S3, supplement unavailable)
experiments.control: other CAR/Sfp expression configurations (details in Table S3)
experiments.outcome: IPB05 showed highest CAR activity and was chosen as route B verification chassis
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate expression-configuration engineering (chromosomal integration + plasmid). Q2: constructed in this paper. Q3: IPB05 became the chassis for IPB06/IPB07.

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Expression balancing of CAR and its activating enzyme Sfp across chromosome (J23105-driven sfp) and plasmid (pTrc-car) to maximize functional CAR.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: CAR activity depended on the CAR:Sfp expression ratio; the initial pCDFDuet coexpression (IPB01) was suboptimal for the production host context.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Based on measured CAR activities across configurations (Table S3); however Table S3 is in the unavailable supplement, so the comparison cannot be independently verified from the main text.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The need for Sfp-mediated activation and its tuning follows the cited literature (ref 22); the specific J23105/pTrc configuration choice is empirical optimization without a stated mechanistic model.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a CAR-dependent pathway is moved to a production host, tune the expression ratio of CAR to its phosphopantetheinyl transferase (e.g., chromosomal constitutive sfp plus plasmid-borne car), because CAR activity is limited by the balance of apo-CAR and its activating enzyme; validated only for CAR/Sfp in E. coli W3110/BL21(DE3).
alternatives_considered: Alternative CAR/Sfp expression configurations listed in Table S3 (supplement unavailable)

experiments.purpose: Achieve de novo IPDO production from glucose via route B
experiments.host: E. coli W3110 chr::J23105-sfp; IPB06 (pTrc-cgh), IPB07 (IPB06 + p15-leu-acd), IPB08 (IPB06 + empty p15AS, negative control)
experiments.intervention: pTrc-cgh (car+GRE2+AaHPD) pathway plasmid; then overexpression of leuAfbrBCD (E. coli), alsS (B. subtilis) and ilvCD (E. coli) on p15AS to enhance alpha-KIC supply
experiments.conditions: FM-II medium, 0.1 mM IPTG at OD600 0.4-0.6, 30 C, 200 rpm, 48 h, shake flask
experiments.readout: IPDO titer (GC and GC-MS confirmation with standard and 1,3-PDO internal standard)
experiments.outcome: IPB06: no IPDO detected. IPB07: 2.2 mg/L IPDO from glucose. IPB08: no IPDO.
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate precursor-supply engineering (leuAfbrBCD/alsS/ilvCD overexpression). Q2: constructed in this paper. Q3: converted a non-producing strain into a producing one, establishing route B in vivo.

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor and flux supply enhancement: overexpress the feedback-resistant leucine operon and upstream BCAA-pathway genes to raise the alpha-KIC pool feeding route B.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: IPB06 carrying the complete route B produced no detectable IPDO from glucose; authors hypothesized that the supply of the precursor alpha-KIC is insufficient (consistent with efficient competing conversion of alpha-KIC to leucine by endogenous IlvE).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Measured outcome: IPB07 produced 2.2 mg/L IPDO while the empty-vector control IPB08 produced none (GC + GC-MS verified).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The intervention directly follows a stated mechanistic hypothesis (precursor alpha-KIC limitation), later reinforced in the Discussion by kinetic comparison of IlvE (Km 0.08 mM, kcat 24.7 s-1) versus HPD (Km 0.32 mM, kcat 6.5 min-1) competing for alpha-KIC.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When an alpha-KIC-diverting heterologous pathway in E. coli yields no detectable product despite functional pathway enzymes, enhance precursor supply by overexpressing the feedback-resistant leucine biosynthesis operon (leuAfbrBCD) together with alsS and ilvCD, because the endogenous high-efficiency transaminase IlvE drains the alpha-KIC pool toward leucine; validated only at proof-of-concept level (2.2 mg/L IPDO) in E. coli W3110.

experiments.purpose: Implement route C (alpha,beta-DHIV -> IPDO via CAR, PDDH/YqhD, GDHt) in vitro and in vivo
experiments.host: E. coli BL21(DE3), strains IPC01 (pCDF-car-sfp + pCOLA-yqhD-dhaB) and IPC02 (system-engineered IPC01)
experiments.intervention: heterologous expression of car, sfp, yqhD, dhaB (GDHt from Klebsiella); then system metabolic engineering to increase alpha,beta-DHIV flux and block BCAA pathways (Figure S3, supplement unavailable)
experiments.conditions: in vivo: FM-II, 48 h cultivation; in vitro: 25 mM alpha,beta-DHIV, CAR 1 h then YqhD+DhaB 3 h
experiments.control: BA positive control for CAR activity
experiments.readout: IPDO (GC); CAR activity on alpha,beta-DHIV (0.093 umol/min/mg)
experiments.outcome: CAR active on alpha,beta-DHIV in vitro but <half of BA activity; no IPDO from IPC01, IPC02, or the in vitro cascade
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate engineering (pathway construction; precursor enhancement + competing-pathway blocking in IPC02). Q2: performed here. Q3: represents a strategy choice (precursor supply + competition removal), even though it failed.

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Precursor supply enhancement combined with competitive-pathway removal: increase flux through the alpha,beta-DHIV biosynthesis pathway and block branched-chain amino acid pathways draining it.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: IPC01 carrying route C produced no detectable IPDO after 48 h; alpha,beta-DHIV is efficiently consumed by endogenous IlvD, and CAR shows low affinity/activity toward alpha,beta-DHIV.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Negative GC results are direct measurements; however the specific genetic modifications of IPC02 are only in Figure S3 (supplement unavailable), so the intervention content cannot be fully verified.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The stated logic (raise precursor flux, block competing BCAA consumption) is mechanistic, but the intervention failed to yield IPDO, so the mechanism-to-outcome link is not validated.

experiments.purpose: Implement route D (MVA -> IPDO via CAR and ADO) in E. coli
experiments.host: E. coli BL21(DE3), strain IPD01 (pCDF-car-sfp + pCOLA-af: ado from Prochlorococcus marinus, fdx from Synechocystis sp. 6803, fnr from E. coli)
experiments.intervention: heterologous expression of car, sfp, ado, fdx, fnr (fdx/fnr to supply NADPH for ADO); glucose + MVA cosubstrate cultivation
experiments.conditions: FM-II medium, glucose + MVA cosubstrates, 48 h
experiments.control: BA positive control for CAR activity on MVA (in vitro)
experiments.outcome: CAR active on MVA in vitro; IPD01 produced no detectable IPDO even with MVA supplementation (GC detection limit <1 mg/L)
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate pathway construction including an NADPH-supply module (fdx/fnr) for ADO. Q2: performed here. Q3: tests the route D strategy; failure motivated subsequent enzyme engineering.

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Pathway implementation with cofactor supply design: assemble route D including a ferredoxin/ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase module to feed NADPH to ADO.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Route D was the in silico-designed alternative using pyruvate/MVA as precursor; ADO requires reducing equivalents, motivating fdx/fnr coexpression.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Negative in vivo GC result is a direct measurement; the design rationale for fdx/fnr is stated in text.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The fdx/fnr module follows an explicit mechanistic requirement (NADPH supply for the ADO-catalyzed reaction); the overall route choice, however, relied partly on predictive MDF analysis.

experiments.purpose: Improve CAR activity on alpha,beta-DHIV and MVA (and GDHt/ADO activities) to rescue routes C and D
experiments.host: in vitro (purified CAR mutants) and E. coli route-D strains
experiments.intervention: computational saturation mutagenesis/virtual screening and structure-guided rational design of CAR (binding pocket and adjacent loop residues); rational protein design of GDHt and ADO (Figures S4, S5)
experiments.conditions: in vitro CAR activity assay on MVA; mutants introduced into route D in place of wild-type CAR
experiments.readout: relative CAR activity on MVA; in vivo IPDO
experiments.outcome: Most CAR mutants showed increased activity on MVA; best mutant N227A reached 2.28-fold of wild type in vitro; no CAR, GDHt or ADO mutant enabled IPDO production in vivo
experiments.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate enzyme engineering. Q2: performed here. Q3: mutants were deployed into route D strains, a new design iteration (which nonetheless failed in vivo).

ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Rate-limiting enzyme engineering: structure-guided mutation of CAR binding-pocket and loop residues to improve activity on non-native substrates MVA and alpha,beta-DHIV.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: CAR showed poor catalytic activity on alpha,beta-DHIV (0.093 umol/min/mg) and MVA relative to its native substrate BA, identified as a key reason for routes C/D failure; CAR's known substrate-preference rule (second functional group at least three carbons from carboxylate) explains the poor fit.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: In vitro mutant activities were measured (Figure 4b; N227A 2.28-fold); the preceding virtual screening is predictive (soft) but was confirmed by in vitro assays. In vivo rescue failed.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Mutagenesis targeted the binding pocket and adjacent loop based on the CAR crystal structure, an explicit structure-mechanism-guided rationale.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When CAR shows poor activity on a non-native carboxylic acid substrate, apply structure-guided saturation mutagenesis of binding-pocket and adjacent loop residues, because these positions shape substrate accommodation; validated only in vitro for MVA (N227A, 2.28-fold) and did not rescue in vivo IPDO production, so transfer to in vivo pathway contexts is unproven.
